title: fix(skill-core): class a gh api call that adds a parameter as a change
body:
Closes #68

`is_read` now decides a `gh api` call's method as gh does: the last `-X` or `--method`, or else POST when a parameter is added, in each spelling gh reads (`-f`, `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`, joined, after `=`, and in a cluster after `-i`), and GET otherwise.

## Upgrade note

None.

## Validation

Siblings: searched gh api's options for every one that adds a parameter; `-f`, `-F`, and their long forms are all of them, and each spelling has a test.

closing_issues.title: github_client retries a gh api call that adds a parameter, which gh sends as a POST
closing_issues.body:
## What and why

`is_read` in `skills/ejryan89-skill-core/scripts/github_client.py` decides which gh commands `run` may retry after a transient failure, and its module docstring promises that a request that may change something on GitHub is never retried. It classes a `gh api` call by the method it names alone, so a call that names none is a read. gh sends such a call as a POST when it adds a parameter.

## Reproduction

```python
>>> is_read(["api", "repos/o/r/issues", "-f", "title=Flaky"])
True
```

gh sent it as a POST and created the issue. A 502 after GitHub had applied it was retried, and the issue was created twice.

## Expected

`is_read` is false for every `gh api` call gh sends with a method other than GET, decided as gh decides the method, so no request that changes something on GitHub is retried.
